measures.what: the mounting platform where the missing part sat: is it a metal stud sticking UP out of the platform, or a threaded HOLE in the platform? Tell me which, plus the stud's or hole's diameter, and if a stud, how far it sticks up above the platform surface. Also the flat platform's width across.
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above

measures.what: the tripod socket on the bottom: the inner diameter of the threaded hole, and how deep the thread runs (poke a drill bit or a small screw in until it stops, mark it with your fingernail, measure that length). Also the distance from the socket to the nearest edge of the camera's base.
measures.reply: camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.item: the salvaged 1/4-20 bolt from the webcam mount
measures.what: overall length (head to tip), head diameter, head height (how thick), and whether the head has an Allen/hex socket or is a regular hex or round head
measures.reply: webcam bolt head across: about 15 mm (its head); webcam bolt head height: about 5 mm (its head); webcam bolt length: about 10 mm (under the head)

measures.what: the gap between the two jaw faces, measured across the slot the plate drops into: (a) with the knob fully OPEN, and (b) with the knob fully CLOSED. Measure at the level of the lips that do the gripping, in mm.
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above

measures.what: the shape of the gripping lips: are the faces parallel (straight slot) or angled in like a dovetail? How deep are the lips front-to-back (the height of the gripping band), and how far apart are the lips along the plate's travel direction? If you can press a lump of blu-tack or playdough into the gap and lay the imprint flat, tell me the profile's key numbers.
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above

measures.what: the flat area on the bottom around the tripod socket: its length x width in mm, and how far the socket centre is from the nearest edge of that flat area (this is how big my plate may be before it hangs off the camera). Also roughly how heavy the whole thing is.
measures.reply: camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

measures.what: the head's drive: is it a hex/Allen socket (if so, the width across the socket), a hex head (width across flats), or a round knurled head? And is the head's underside flat or rounded?
measures.reply: webcam bolt head across: about 15 mm (its head); webcam bolt head height: about 5 mm (its head)

measures.what: with the knob wound all the way open, the clear distance between the two jaw lips' inner faces (this is the widest thing the plate may be), and how deep the slot is between the jaws from the top of the clamp down
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above

measures.what: the flat top surface of the clamp that the plate's underside rests on: width across and length, and the width across the two angled lips measured with a ruler straight across the slot
measures.reply: tripod clamp style: jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above

measures.what: the flat patch on the underside around the 1/4-20 socket: length x width in mm, and how far the socket centre sits from the nearest edge of that flat patch
measures.reply: camera socket thread: 1/4-20 (the usual camera thread)

limitations.wanted: The clamp's actual grip dimensions: jaw gap open and closed, the lip depth/angle, and how deep the slot is below the platform the plate rests on
limitations.blocked_by: the measure tool would only return the two cached answers it already gave ('jaws with angled lips, tightened by a knob; the plate drops in from above' and 'camera socket thread: 1/4-20') no matter how the request was rephrased
limitations.why: Those numbers set the plate's foot width, neck width and total grip thickness. Guessing them is the only way a printed plate either won't drop in or will sit loose in the jaws

limitations.wanted: A true helical 1/4-20 thread modelled on the printed spare screw (a profile swept along a helix), and a countersunk/shoulder seat so the screw is captive in the plate like a real quick-release plate
limitations.blocked_by: no thread/helix helper I could rely on compiling in the submission's CadQuery code, and no captive-screw hardware in the list (the only 1/4-20 male part is the salvaged bolt, whose 15 mm head is too fat to snap through a printed throat)
limitations.why: A real helical thread screws in smoothly and doesn't stress the camera's steel socket; a captive screw stops the plate falling off the camera once it's off the tripod
